fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. God tells Ezekiel, “…write down today’s date…” I would have checked the calendar three times and still written it in pencil, just to be safe. God gives the reason right away: on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.

A list of names sounds so official, friend. I can almost see the clipboard. But the instruction in verse 2 is, “…write down today’s date…” God follows it with the reason: on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.

I'd love a song here too, friend, but that's not what God says. He tells Ezekiel, “…write down today’s date…” The verse names a date, not a song. Then God gives the reason: on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.
Nineveh is a good guess, friend, but it's not the city named here. God says that on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem. That's the city in the text.
Damascus is a fair guess, baker, but it isn't named here. God tells Ezekiel that on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem. That's the city the date belongs to.

True, baker. God says, “Take the choicest of the flock and pile the fuel beneath it. Bring it to a boil and cook the bones in it.” The fuel goes under the pot first, and then comes the boil. I've never been so glad my ovens come with a timer.
On the bare rock, baker. God says, “she poured it out on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.” Bare rock has nothing to cover it. This is a heavy part, friend.

The Jordan is a famous river, friend, but it isn't in this verse. God says the blood was poured out “…on the bare rock…” He also says it wasn't poured on the ground to cover it with dust. It's a heavy part of the passage.

A city gate feels like a natural spot, friend, but the text never says it. God says the city “…poured it out on the bare rock…” The verse also says she didn't pour it on the ground to cover it with dust. This is one of the heavy parts.
That's what God says, baker. His words are, “In order to stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have placed her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.” This is a heavy verse, friend.

Warning the nations sounds like a reasonable purpose, friend, but the text doesn't say it. God gives His own reason: “…to stir up wrath and take vengeance…” The nations aren't mentioned in these verses at all.
Burned is the word, baker. God says, “let the bones be burned.” Just before that, He says to pile on the logs and kindle the fire.
True, baker. God says, “I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent.” It follows right after “the time is coming, and I will act.” This is a heavy line.
The text says it the other way, friend. God says, “I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent.” That's what He says in verse 14. It's a heavy line.
Right, baker. God says, “I will judge you according to your ways and deeds…” That's how He closes the parable. It's a heavy ending.
